ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: This figure is a schematic diagram of the distribution of near-surface wind belts in a hemisphere. The figure has latitude labels such as 0°, 30°, 60°, and 90° and wind direction arrows; the letter b is located in the upper right part of the figure, near the subtropical region around the 30° latitude line. Reasoning: According to the distribution law of global pressure belts and wind belts, the vicinity of 30° corresponds to the subtropical high-pressure belt, where descending air currents prevail, water vapor is not easy to condense, and precipitation is low; at the same time, this latitude is relatively low and heat conditions are sufficient. Therefore the climate feature at b is hot and dry.
